question: Does physical row/column removal implement the same MLP function as zeroing the same full-width up rows? This investigates whether width handling explains the already observed pruning losses; it does not reopen the failed size gate.
control: Retain original tensor shapes, scales and down weights. Independently zero only the removed up-weight rows. Recheck all masked tensors and the previously generated pruned containers against their exact intended tensors.
kernel_cases: 16 layers x 1024 fixed synthetic inputs per candidate. Seed 0x92f375ab; biased-u8 extremes, centered zero, alternating extremes and xorshift inputs. Use actual recorded native kernels and compiler flags; force both sparse and dense down routes.
acceptance: Retained quantized activations match exactly after index mapping
Sparse and dense residual float outputs match bit for bit
Unmasked original versus pruned must fail via a semantic mismatch exit, not a crash or timeout
limits: Synthetic block evidence only; no proof for every input, full transformer, full arithmetic coder or prize submission. The original unmasked model is intentionally not equivalent to pruning. Existing rejected fixture results remain rejected.
followup: If masked and pruned kernels disagree, locate the mismatch before interpreting pruning as a clean model intervention. If all agree, prioritize measured activations or training over more weight-norm pruning sweeps.
